summary: The support-function separation proves the simultaneous-packing/max-affine equivalence with attainment, Jensen's inequality and the max-affine test prove the nonnegative convex-order equivalence, and the leaf reduction proves the tree criterion. The cube construction has the stated masses and moments; the extremal first-coordinate argument proves slab uniqueness; the affine certificate gives both failure of unit-capacity packing and the sharp congestion lower bound; and the selected closed halfspace gives the claimed domination bound. The arguments also cover the stated boundary and d=1 cases.
